_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. The mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so the (non-)oracle registration and the catalog live here. `s.note.note` is a semio-NATIVE artifact persisted as `.dsl.semio` text and `.pack.semio` binary through this subset's own codecs; no third party reads or writes either, so no oracle is registered — see noOracleDecisions below.

oracles.rationale:
A second implementation of the `s.note.note` document and all thirty-three typed mutations, in Python, at `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-note-1/🐍️component.py`. Written from `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️component.json` (the document's members and the six block kinds), rules 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7 of `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL/📓️derivation-rules.md` — including rule 5's `move-to-<container>` for re-parenting and rule 7's absolute `move`/`resize` against relative `drag` — and the thirty-three committed `(before, mutation, after, outcome)` vectors, which are the only statement of five things: that `drag-blocks` translates a named block AND ITS WHOLE SUBTREE; that `delete-asset` removes the `assets` MEMBER outright when it empties the table; that `insert-table-column` names the appended column by its spreadsheet letter; that the two `insert-table-*` verbs append BLANK cells, which is what makes their inverses exact against the committed trailing-blank vectors; and how `duplicate-blocks` places its copies. It imports nothing from this repository and transliterates none of its Rust. This registration SUPERSEDES the `note-document-mutation-semantics` no-oracle decision, whose argument was refuted in this same wave by `mutate-semio-drawing`, `mutate-semio-mesh` and the fifteen `📕️norm` references, all of which took Python second implementations over this same carrier. A THIRD-PARTY library was declined, not merely absent: no canvas or whiteboard format models a z-ORDERED tree whose leaves are six differently-shaped typed blocks reached by different verbs, and none of them reads this carrier. TWO FINDINGS THE REFERENCE MADE WHILE BEING WRITTEN. First, `duplicate-blocks` computes each copy's insertion index against the PRE-MUTATION list and does not re-base it as earlier copies land: its committed vector duplicates `blk-ink` (root index 1) and `blk-table` (root index 2) in one mutation, and the committed after-snapshot orders the root `blk-text, blk-ink, blk-ink-copy, blk-table-COPY, blk-table, …` — the second copy lands BEFORE its own source, where the singular `duplicate-block` places its copy after. The reference reproduces the committed order and names the behaviour rather than quietly re-basing it. Second, the committed grammar and the committed artifact disagree, which is why `identity-round-trip` is refused below. THREE SCENARIOS THE REFERENCE REFUSES BY CLAUSE, and says so in role. `edit-block-text` in both roles: a text block does not hold its paragraphs, it holds a composed child handle into an `s.stdio.semio@v1/text` document, and the committed vector's whole observable effect is that handle's `childId` moving to a content address of the child AFTER the new paragraphs are written — a function no document in this repository states. Every OTHER verb over that same block is implemented. And `identity-round-trip`: unlike its `✒️writer`, `🌿️vcs` and `🔌️wires` siblings this subset commits a REAL grammar rather than the repository-wide `payload = OCTET+` placeholder, and grammar and artifact disagree on three points — `block = text-block | image-block | shape-block` covers three of the SIX declared block kinds, leaving stroke, table, math and group with no production at all; `block-field` names `paragraphs` and `asset-id` while the artifact writes neither and writes `content=child_id=… target="…"`, a flattened nested record nothing bounds; and `artifact-mark = "note.note"` is contradicted by the artifact's own first line `semio note.note.dsl v1`. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation needs no distribution, so this entry contributes nothing to `🔒️dependencies.json`.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `note-1-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 33-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.

🖊️ THE CARRIER READER for note's DXF export, and already the qualifying reference `s.stdio.dxf@r12/✳️any` registers under `dxf-crate-r12-mutate` (this repository's `🔒️dependencies.json`) — reused here for the SAME crate reading the SAME `print_dxf_document` text this subset's own `NoteIntoDxf` serializer calls (`../🚪️io/📤️export/🧵️serializers/🗿️artifacts/🖊️dxf/🔖️r12/✳️any/🦀️component.rs`), so nothing new is being asked of `dxf` — only a second registration of an already-qualified crate against a second subset's vocabulary.

WHAT IT CAN AND CANNOT WITNESS, read from the serializer's own body rather than assumed. `NoteIntoDxf::serialize` walks `flatten_blocks(&from.blocks)` and emits a `DxfEntity::Line` for every consecutive pair of an `Ink` block's OWN `points` array — nothing else: `if let NoteBlockNode::Ink { points, .. } = block { for pair in points.windows(2) { entities.push(DxfEntity::Line { start: [pair[0][0], pair[0][1], 0.0], end: [pair[1][0], pair[1][1], 0.0], layer: "0".into(), unknown_group_codes: Vec::new() }); } }`. Three consequences, each MEASURED against the serializer body rather than guessed: (1) `points` are written RAW, with no `block.x`/`block.y`/`rotation` transform applied anywhere in this function — so `move-block`, `drag-blocks`, `resize-block` and `move-block-to-container` produce byte-IDENTICAL DXF output regardless of the mutation; only `edit-block-ink-stroke` (which rewrites `points` itself) and existence changes (`create-block`/`delete-block`/`delete-blocks`/`duplicate-block`/`duplicate-blocks` when they add or remove an Ink block) are witnessable. (2) `flatten_blocks` is never filtered by `block_visible` here — unlike the SVG bridge below — so `change-block-visible`/`change-block-locked` leave the DXF output unchanged even though the block visually disappears in SVG; this is a genuine cross-carrier inconsistency in the subject, not a limitation of the oracle, and is reported rather than worked around. (3) the `Line` entity carries no width/color field, so `change-block-ink-width` is invisible here (it IS visible via the SVG carrier's stroke-width style). Every other block kind (Text/Image/Table/Math/Group) and every document-root setting (grid/snap/pencil/eraser/rename-note) never reaches this serializer at all.

productionDebt.plan: n/a — dxf is test-only everywhere it is linked

engine.implementation: quick-xml pull-parser over the SVG 1.1 XML this subset exports

oracles.rationale:
🎨️ THE RICHEST CARRIER for this subset. `NoteIntoSvg::serialize` (`../🚪️io/📤️export/🧵️serializers/🗿️artifacts/🎨️svg/🔖️1.1/✳️any/🦀️component.rs`) delegates to `note_document_to_svg`, a REAL bridge (never a hand-rolled string): `note_document_to_drawing_snapshot` (`../🚪️io/🦀️component.rs`) walks `flatten_blocks(&document.blocks).filter(|b| block_visible(b))` — visibility IS honoured here, unlike the DXF path above — and wraps every surviving block's shape in `DrawNode::Group { transform: note_block_transform(block), .. }`, where `note_block_transform` reads the block's OWN `x`/`y`/`rotation` into a real translate+rotate transform. `write_svg_xml` then prints that transform as the `<g transform="…">` this probe reads back with quick-xml.

PER-BLOCK-KIND WITNESSABILITY, read from `draw_node_from_note_block`. `Ink` → a real `<path>` (stroke geometry AND `stroke-width`, so `edit-block-ink-stroke` and `change-block-ink-width` are BOTH witnessable here, the second only here). `Text` → a real `<text>` element holding the joined paragraph text (`edit-block-text` witnessable) BUT `font_size` is wired to the glyph's `y` COORDINATE (`at: SemioPoint2 { x: 0.0, y: *font_size }`), never to a font-size style property — `change-block-font-size` therefore moves the baseline rather than changing any rendered size, a genuine subject bug this oracle exposes rather than one it can quietly confirm, so it is registered as unsupported/excluded from this mutation despite being numerically visible. `Image` → a real `<image>` with the asset's own bytes when the referenced asset exists (`create-asset`/`replace-asset-payload`/`delete-asset` witnessable ONLY when a visible Image block references that asset key), else a generic outline rectangle. `Table`/`Math`/`Group` → ALWAYS a generic gray outline rectangle keyed only to `width`/`height` — cell/formula CONTENT is invisible by construction (`edit-block-math` and the four table row/column verbs are un-witnessable here because their diffs mutate `rows`/`columns`/`cells`, never `width`/`height` — confirmed by reading `insert-table-row`'s own diff). `change-block-locked`, `rename-block` and `rename-note` have no rendered representation anywhere in this bridge.

productionDebt.plan: n/a — quick-xml is test-only everywhere it is linked

oracles.rationale:
📄️ `lopdf` is ALREADY an approved test-oracle in this repository (`🔒️dependencies.json` — capabilities `pdf-edit`/`pdf-parse`, linked into the very crate `../../../../../../../../✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🧪️oracle/📦️packages/🦀️rust/Cargo.toml` this registration reuses); this entry is a second registration of that crate against `note-1-mutate` rather than a new dependency.

`NoteIntoPdf::serialize` (`../🚪️io/📤️export/🧵️serializers/🗿️artifacts/📄️pdf/🔖️1.4/✳️any/🦀️component.rs`) flattens the document's `title` (if any) followed by EVERY `Text` block's paragraph runs, space-joined, onto ONE `PdfPage.text` field of a single-page `PdfSnapshot` — real page geometry (`PageDoc`/`w`/`h`) and a real `encode_pdf`, never a stub. Two consequences read directly from that body: (1) `rename-note` IS witnessable here — the title is the first thing concatenated — even though it is invisible to both DXF and SVG. (2) exactly like the DXF path, `flatten_blocks` here is never filtered by `block_visible`, so `change-block-visible` on a Text block leaves the PDF text unchanged (the same cross-carrier inconsistency the DXF entry reports, independently confirmed on a second serializer). Position, block existence order beyond concatenation order, and every non-Text block kind (Ink/Image/Table/Math/Group) are invisible: the serializer never reads their fields at all.

comparisonProfiles.description: note→DXF compared by the SET of Line entities' (start,end) coordinate pairs the Ink blocks produce. Layer name, group codes and entity order are writer freedom. Position/rotation/visibility/lock/width are NOT carried by this serializer and are out of this profile's scope by construction.

note→SVG compared by each surviving (visible) block's kind, its <g transform="…"> translate+rotate, and kind-specific content: Ink path d + stroke-width, Text joined value, Image mime+bytes when a referenced asset exists, Table/Math/Group outline width/height. Style ids, path command formatting and XML attribute order are writer freedom.

note→PDF compared by the single page's extracted text stream (title + space-joined Text block runs, in document order) and page width/height. Object numbers, xref layout, compression and PDF producer metadata are writer freedom.
